newsitem.title: MACAU: China warns southern river poisoned with cyanide.
newsitem.headline: China warns southern river poisoned with cyanide.

text.p: Authorities in southern China have issued a poison alert in the Pearl River delta following reports that cynanide spilled into a tributary, the Macau government and Chinese local authorities said on Wednesday.
Officials in Portuguese-ruled Macau off the south China coast, and in the Chinese city of Zhuhai just across the border, said they were monitoring the situation closely.

A Macau water company spokesman said there was "no cause for alarm" yet, but water analysis had been stepped up after the warning from China's Guangxi province that potassium cyanide had polluted a river in the region.
A spokesman at the Zhuhai city hall said public departments, hotels and the population of about 430,000 had been advised not to use untreated water from the West River and tributaries.
Chinese sources in Macau told Reuters a car carrying potassium cyanide had recently fallen into a river in Guangxi province that flows into the South China Sea, west of Macau.
They also said the chemical released in the accident, which took place about 200 km (125 miles) from Macau, would take about three days to reach the waters around the enclave.
The Urban Council and water company assured residents most of Macau's tap water, which comes comes from Zhuhai, was safe.
